title: The Bedrock Choir Where Epochs Learn to Sing

features.name: the singing shaft
features.desc-on-touch: stone walls carved by water and time ring with frequencies you can't quite hear — the archive installed equipment here to listen to epochs singing their own sedimentation back.

features.name: settling pools
features.desc-on-touch: three small chambers where mineral-rich water pooled and waited; each one holds a different frequency of silence.

features.name: the old installation
features.desc-on-touch: concrete foundation where the archive's first sensor array lived; the concrete has learned to resonate — cracks run like musical staffs.

features.name: epoch markers
features.desc-on-touch: stone faces scored with silent numbers — each layer of the bedrock singing a different age at frequencies the archive tries to translate.

features.name: listening chamber
features.desc-on-touch: a carved alcove where sound becomes geology; equipment here draws the deep tones out of stone and stores them as numbers that smell like rust.

inscription: epochs learn to sing only after they have finished falling

file.name: Bedrock_Resonance_Profile_NSW_20yrs.mp3
file.note: 300 hours of deep-frequency recordings; the file corrupted slowly, each re-download arriving pitched differently — the archive is learning to sing in minor keys

reverie.title: REVERIE — bedrock's patient counting
narr: you knelt in the chamber while she arranged the
microphone arms. stone cold against your palms.
she said: listen — it's been singing for
fifty million years, we're just first to pay
attention. you held still. the earth hummed.
her hands moved the equipment; yours stayed.

exits.label: back up through mineral light to where seeds know time
into a shaft where echoes learn to echo themselves
toward a deeper chamber where the archive first broke ground
down toward where the singing grows older still
